notes: Perfect match on all claims (C51, C52, C56, C57, C58). Both agree that MD simulations successfully validated against dEGFR crystal structures, reproducing gap formation in ligand-free dimers.
Perfect match on all claims (C113, C114, C115). Both agree on reproducibility of simulations, with peer reviewers explicitly praising this as 'remarkable' for such large systems.

Strong overlap (5/6 claims: C100, C101, C103, C126, C127). Both accept the general mechanism that domain II conformation is critical and regulated by ligand binding, though peer reviewers request more mechanistic detail.

Strong overlap (7/11 shared claims). Both agree on the key finding that single ligand stabilizes Her2 heterodimers. Peer review includes additional claims (C10, C44, C82, C83) but maintains SUPPORTED status for the core finding.

Partial overlap (2/4 claims: C106, C129). Both agree on evolutionary conservation of dimerization mechanism from Drosophila to human. LLM includes C11 while peer includes C50, but both reach SUPPORTED conclusion.

Overlap on C84, C85, C86 (atomic-level interactions). LLM finds conserved interactions sufficiently detailed and SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers criticize lack of mechanistic detail and rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'authors unfortunately give no details for the analogous interfaces.'

Overlap on C93, C94, C97, C98 regarding Her2-specific interactions and missing arginine. Both agree the mechanistic explanation is speculative and requires experimental validation. LLM notes 'causal link...remains speculative' while peer wants 'more definitive analysis.'

Both address C99 (L291R mutation prediction). LLM rates UNSUPPORTED as 'purely speculative and not tested,' while peer rates UNCERTAIN, suggesting analysis could provide insight. Disagreement on whether speculation merits UNCERTAIN vs UNSUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap (C87, C88 on Arg228/Glu243 interactions). LLM finds Her2-specific interactions SUPPORTED, but peer reviewers group these with broader interface analysis they find insufficiently detailed (UNCERTAIN).
Minimal overlap (C82, C83 on Her3-Her2 heterodimers). Both agree on ligand-dependent stability pattern. Peer review groups these with broader heterodimer findings but maintains SUPPORTED status.

Minimal overlap (C78 on Her2 homodimer gap formation). LLM finds structural mechanism SUPPORTED, but peer reviewers question whether this provides substantive new explanation beyond Drosophila work, rating UNCERTAIN and stating 'this was already clear from the Drosophila work.'

Minimal overlap (C50 only). LLM addresses asymmetric heterodimer conformations (C10, C50, C66-C69), while peer focuses on evolutionary conservation (C50, C106, C129). Both SUPPORTED but addressing different aspects.
Minimal overlap (C44 only). LLM addresses Her2 homodimer instability mechanism, while peer addresses broader heterodimer stability. Both SUPPORTED but different scopes.
Minimal overlap (C10 only). LLM focuses on asymmetric conformations, peer on heterodimer stability. Both SUPPORTED but addressing different structural aspects.
LLM addresses quantitative buried surface area measurements (C59-C62, C76-C77) with SUPPORTED status. No direct peer review match, though related to interface analysis discussed in peer R4 and R6.
LLM addresses quantitative domain II bending angle measurements (C71-C73) with SUPPORTED status. No direct peer review match, though related to conformational mechanism accepted in peer R9.
LLM addresses modeling approach justification based on sequence homology (C64-C65, C107-C109) with SUPPORTED status. Not explicitly addressed in peer review results.

Peer review challenges characterization of Her3-Her2 heterodimers as 'particularly robust' (C17), questioning strength and prevalence claims. No corresponding LLM result addresses this specific claim.
